Found by the second credentialed #653 verify (2026-08-08, head 6ece9f9): the gate's capture/checkpoint scenarios fail with the provider's NEW actionable refusal —

> session_start bound the lane to namespace 'ob-admin', not the configured 'eval-live-recall-...'. The namespace is carried by OPENBRAIN_NAMESPACE and is never a request key; to bind a namespace your token does not already grant, set OPENBRAIN_DELEGATE_NAMESPACE=1 with an admin/ob-admin token so the request sends the X-Namespace header. Nothing was written to '...'.

This is #657's opt-in default-OFF and #662's error text both working as designed. The defect: `eval/open-brain/live/scenario-transport.ts:109-119` spawns `uv run openbrain-memory` with only OPENBRAIN_BASE_URL/TOKEN/NAMESPACE/PROJECT — no delegation flag — while always deriving a per-run namespace the token does not already grant.

Operator ruling (ledger item 30.1): the TRANSPORT owns the delegation request — it sets OPENBRAIN_DELEGATE_NAMESPACE=1 in the spawned provider env, with a comment carrying the reason (a component that derives foreign namespaces always needs the header). NOT in live-eval.env.

Done-means design (red-first, hermetic where possible): (a) unit-level — the transport's provider env contains OPENBRAIN_DELEGATE_NAMESPACE=1 (RED today; assert the env construction, pattern: eval unit tests assert call shapes per the repo convention); (b) control — the other four env keys unchanged; (c) mutation — remove the flag, clause (a) fails.
